audit_findings.title: FY2025 owner earnings do not include the full recurring interest burden of the latest capital structure
audit_findings.magnitude: net effect unquantified; $205.0 million incremental debt at the June 2026 rate of 6.89% implies $14.1 million of annual pretax interest, equal to 14.7% of the $96.1 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: A recurring after-tax interest charge remains in equity-level owner earnings and reduces the earnings anchor capitalized by the DCF.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect our interest expense in 2026 to be relatively higher than the amounts incurred in 2025 due to incremental financing activities, but mitigated by proactively securing favorable terms to reduce overall borrowing costs.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated: the incremental term loan was raised on December 16, 2025, so FY2025 includes only a small fraction of its recurring interest, while the bridge reflects the resulting capital structure. The gross run-rate is large relative to the anchor and can materially change intrinsic value. It does not by itself prove the net anchor is overstated by $14.1 million because earnings generated by the financed acquisitions must be included on the same perimeter.
audit_findings.action: Recalculate owner earnings using LTM June 2026 results or a bridge-date pro forma that includes full run-rate after-tax interest and the corresponding acquired-business earnings, maintenance investment, and working-capital needs; rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The earnings anchor and bridge do not share the same acquisition perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 pro-forma common net income exceeded reported common net income by $9.507 million before owner-earnings adjustments; the 2026 acquisition contribution is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The mismatch affects the owner-earnings numerator through acquired earnings, interest, maintenance investment, and working capital while the bridge already reflects acquisition cash use, debt, and liabilities.
audit_findings.evidence: The results for the six businesses acquired during the year have been included in our Consolidated Financial Statements beginning on the respective dates of acquisition.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated. FY2025 contains only post-acquisition results, whereas the June 2026 bridge includes four additional 2026 acquisitions with $135.559 million of consideration. The filed 2025 pro-forma uplift equals 9.9% of the current anchor, which is large enough to matter, but its conversion to owner earnings and the net contribution from the 2026 acquisitions cannot be established from the record. The direction is mixed because acquired operating earnings increase value while financing costs and reinvestment reduce it.
audit_findings.action: Construct LTM June 2026 or acquisition-date pro-forma owner earnings for the complete bridge-date perimeter, including all acquired earnings, incremental interest, maintenance capex, working capital, leases, and contingent consideration, then rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition earn-outs are an omitted senior claim on equity value
audit_findings.magnitude: $29.826 million June 2026 fair-value liability, or $1.82 per diluted share and 1.9% of the $1.577 billion base equity value; maximum payments are $33.0 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Contingent consideration is a separate acquisition claim that should be deducted in the equity bridge to the extent not otherwise captured.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the maximum amount of contingent consideration payable under these arrangements is $ 14.9 million over three years .
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is demonstrated by the June 2026 filing and bridge. Deducting the filed fair-value liability would reduce base value from approximately $96.40 to $94.58 per share. Even the $33.0 million contractual maximum is only about 2.1% of base equity value and would not change the valuation conclusion relative to the $184 market price.
audit_findings.action: Deduct the $29.826 million bridge-date fair-value liability, confirm that no portion is already separately deducted, and update the balance for settlements or remeasurements in the next filing.

audit_findings.title: The entire cash balance may not be distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: required operating cash is unquantified; the exposed add-back is $226.618 million, equal to $13.85 per diluted share and 14.4% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Only cash exceeding operating, contractual, debt-service, and covenant liquidity requirements belongs in the equity bridge; adding required cash double counts capital needed to sustain forecast owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: We also require cash to pay our lease obligations, fund project work-in-process and to service our debt.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that cash supports working capital, project execution, leases, and debt service, but it does not establish the minimum required balance. Therefore, an overstatement is possible but not demonstrated. The full add-back is large enough for the issue to matter, although even removing all $226.618 million would leave base value near $82.55 per share, still below the $184 market price.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a bridge-date cash-uses schedule covering normal working capital, project commitments, restricted or trapped cash, acquisition commitments, debt service, leases, and covenant headroom; add back only the residual excess cash and rerun the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Series B conversion requires a matching numerator adjustment
audit_findings.magnitude: $0.090 million annual preferred dividend; approximately $1.3 million of base equity value or $0.08 per diluted share if omitted from the numerator
audit_findings.mechanism: Using the 840,000 conversion shares requires owner earnings before the Series B dividend; restoring the dividend increases the numerator.
audit_findings.evidence: Each share of the Series B convertible preferred stock is convertible into 56 shares of common stock and a monthly dividend per share of $ 0.50 .
audit_findings.explanation: The filing confirms that diluted EPS adds the dividend back when assuming conversion. Whether the supplied owner-earnings series starts before or after preferred dividends is unresolved, but the maximum identified mismatch is only 0.094% of the $96.1 million anchor and about 0.08% of base equity value, so it cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace each annual owner-earnings numerator to net income or net income attributable to common shareholders; where the latter was used, add back the $90,000 Series B dividend before rerunning.
